primitives.verbatim_quote: After the inquiry had been fairly started it took the form of submitting a certain number of printed questions to a large number of persons.

primitives.name: Question Design Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is hardly any more difficult task than that of framing questions which are not likely to be misunderstood, which admit of easy reply, and which cover the ground of inquiry.
primitives.assumptions: Optimal question design maximizes U ∩ E ∩ C under constraint of cognitive accessibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when U < 0.5 or E < 0.3, leading to invalid inference kernels.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between question structure and information-theoretic channel capacity in cognitive encoding.

primitives.name: Mental Image Characterization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first group of the rather long series of queries related to the illumination, definition, and coloring of the mental image, and were framed thus : ...
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'mental image (vector space of sensory features)', 'L': 'illumination level (luminance units)', 'D': 'definition sharpness (spatial frequency units)', 'C': 'color saturation (spectral intensity units)'}

primitives.breakdown_regime: When I is undefined or non-orthogonal, image reconstruction fails due to perceptual ambiguity.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the statistical inquiry protocol, which formalizes the process of collecting subjective data from multiple individuals. This maps directly to a Bayesian inference kernel where each respondent contributes a sample from a latent cognitive distribution. The question design principle acts as a constraint on the likelihood function, ensuring that the data collected is informative and minimally ambiguous. Mental image characterization provides the feature space for the cognitive variables being inferred. Together, these primitives define a dual structure: a generative model of perception and an observational model of behavior. The failure mode arises when the design principle breaks down, causing information loss or misinterpretation, which leads to invalid posterior estimates in GSI. In GSE, this manifests as a breakdown in situational reasoning when the mental image representation becomes inconsistent or degenerate.
